t: Michael Cristofer
s: Michael Cristofer (born January 22, 1945) is an American playwright, actor, and filmmaker.[1] Cristofer first gained widespread recognition as a playwright with The Shadow Box, a drama that premiered on Broadway in 1977 and examines terminal illness through interconnected stories of patients and their families; the work earned him the Pulitzer Prize for Drama as well as the Tony Award for Best Play.[1][2] Beginning his professional career as a stage actor after training at the Yale School of Drama, he wrote several other plays including Black Angel and The Lady and the Clarinet before shifting focus to screenwriting and directing projects such as the HBO film Gia (1998) and Original Sin (2001).[1] Cristofer resumed acting in the 2000s, appearing in theater productions like A View from the Bridge and television roles including the executive Phillip Price on Mr.
